title: Pairwise distances without loops
prompt:
Write `pairwise_distances(A, B)`: for `A` of shape (n, d) and `B` of shape (m, d), return the (n, m) matrix of Euclidean distances, where entry [i, j] is the distance between row i of A and row j of B. No Python loops.

It must be exactly zero (never NaN) for identical rows, even when rows are huge numbers that differ only slightly.
hints: Give A a new axis so it broadcasts against B: shapes (n, 1, d) and (1, m, d) combine to (n, m, d).

Square the differences, sum over the last axis, then take the square root. The faster identity ‖a‖² + ‖b‖² − 2a·b can go slightly negative from cancellation; if you use it, clip at 0 before the square root.
diff = A[:, None, :] - B[None, :, :]; return np.sqrt((diff ** 2).sum(axis=-1))
